extracted.intended_audience: laboratory students, bacteriologists, and microbiology technicians
extracted.subtask_description: Laboratory protocol and supporting reference material for running trial and final disinfectant (phenol coefficient) tests, preparing dilutions and media, and specific methods (e.g., Antiformin) used in bacteriological practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and numbering of bile-salt broth tubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange 20 tubes of bile salt broth in the upper tier of the test-tube rack in two rows, those in the front row numbered consecutively from left to right 1-10, those in the back row 11-20. For larger tests arrange a further 20 tubes numbered 21-40 in a second smaller rack which can be stood on the upper tier as soon as the first 20 have been inoculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This precise arrangement and numbering is required for consistent sampling and recording during trial and final phenol-coefficient tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for receiving inoculated tubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Place a square wire basket of about 50 tubes capacity close to the left of the test-tube rack for the reception of the inoculated tubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeps inoculated/subculture tubes organized and prevents contamination or mix-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sterile 1 c.c. pipette with rubber washer
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a sterile 1 c.c. pipette, pick up a sterile rubber washer with forceps and push the point of the pipette into the central hole (washer fitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The washer steadies the pipette in the tube mouth and prevents damage; forceps should be used to handle the washer to maintain sterility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positioning pipette in test-tubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Without removing the tube from the rack, remove the cotton-wool plug and lower the pipette with the rubber washer on to the open mouth of the tube; using forceps to steady, push the pipette on through the hole until the point of the pipette has reached to within a few millimetres of the bottom of the tube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once adjusted the pipette may be released; the elastic washer prevents damage. Repeat adjustment for tubes A–E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of pipette/washer in multiple tubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust a sterile 1 c.c. pipette and a washer in the mouth of each of the other tubes, B, C, D and E, in the same way as for tube A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all pipettes are set to the same depth for reproducible sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing by electric signal clock (trial run)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the electric signal clock to ring for the commencement of the experiment and at subsequent intervals of 2-1/2, 5, 25 and 30 minutes (trial runs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict timing is essential to compare contact-period lethality across tubes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing by electric signal clock (final test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the electric signal clock to ring for the commencement of the experiment and subsequently at 2-1/2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 minutes (final test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final test uses denser time points to identify weakest lethal dilutions at short and longer contact periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume of inoculum to prepare
rubrics_metrics.description: Take up 0.5 c.c. of B. coli emulsion in a sterile pipette graduated in tenths of a cubic centimetre and stand by.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precisely graduated pipettes to ensure accurate inoculum volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivering inoculum into germicide solution
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as the bell rings lift the pipette from tube A and deliver 0.1 c.c. of B. coli emulsion into the 1:100 solution; then replace the pipette and washer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform rapidly and consistently for each tube according to schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing germ and germicide
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise the tube with the left hand and shake it to mix germ and germicide immediately after delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shaking ensures uniform contact; the inoculation of the five tubes can be carried out very expeditiously, but allow a period of 10 seconds for each tube.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow 10 seconds per tube for inoculation and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The inoculation of the five tubes can be carried out very expeditiously, but a period of 10 seconds must be allowed for each tube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also note that steps 13–15 occupy on average 10 seconds; timing is critical to maintain contact-period integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling technique at contact times (blowing through pipette)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the bell rings at 2-1/2 minutes blow through the pipette in tube A to agitate the germ+germicide mixture and ensure collection of a fair sample; allow the mixture to enter the pipette and, as the column extends well above the terminal graduation, adjust the right forefinger over the butt-end to retain more than 0.1 c.c., then touch the point on the inner wall to allow excess to escape so only 0.1 c.c. is retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique ensures a reproducible 0.1 c.c. sample from contact-period tube; attention to pipette graduation and finger technique is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous transfer to subculture (step sequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the same time remove Bile Salt Tube No. 1 from the rack, take out the cotton-wool plug with the hand already holding the pipette, insert the point of the pipette into the subculture tube, and blow out the mixture into the medium; replug the tube and drop it into the wire basket. Replace the washer-pipette in the original tube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative positions of pipette, plug and culture tube should mirror established technique (cf. earlier figures). Steps 13–15 average 10 seconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat sampling for each tube and at each scheduled interval
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat steps 13, 14 and 15 with each of the other tubes B, C, D and E, and repeat these steps when the bell rings at 5, 25 and 30 minutes (trial) or at the full set of times in the final test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure identical procedure and timing for all tubes to make lethality comparisons valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incubation conditions for subcultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Place all the inoculated tubes in the incubator at 37 deg. C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strict incubation temperature for growth detection; Table 27 gives typical incubation times (e.g., 7 days at 37°C for many entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination schedule and recording of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the tubes at intervals of 24 hours, and record the results in tabular form (figures in the squares indicate the number of hours at which changes in the medium due to growth of B. coli first appeared).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record first appearance of growth (hours) per tube; use the tabular format (example provided) for clarity and for deciding lethal dilutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision rule for proceeding to final test
rubrics_metrics.description: If tabulated results indicate strengths of Germicide-x lethal at 2-1/2 and 30 minutes the final test can be arranged; if not, use available evidence to plan a second trial test to obtain the required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trial run identifies approximate lethal strengths; final test requires those strengths to bracket lethal points at both short and long contact times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final test setup for X-disinfectant (five strengths)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange five test-tubes clearly marked in the lower tier of the rack and pipette into each 5 c.c. respectively of the five percentage solutions of x-disinfectant which the trial run has already shown will include those affording lethal values at 2-1/2 and 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final test uses five graded strengths chosen from the trial run to determine the weakest lethal dilutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control phenol experiment (identical method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately the subculture tubes from the 30-minute contact period have been inoculated, carry out a precisely similar experiment in which five percentage strengths of Phenol (e.g., 1.1, 1.0, 0.9, 0.75, 0.7) are arranged in the lower tier in place of the five strengths of Germicide-x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control phenol must be carried out under identical conditions to provide a reference for calculation of phenol coefficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phenol coefficient calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the phenol coefficient by: (a) divide the percentage strength of the weakest lethal dilution of the carbolic acid control at the 2-1/2-minute contact period by that of the x-disinfectant at the same period (phenol coefficient at 2-1/2 min); (b) obtain similarly for 30 minutes; (c) record the mean of the two coefficients obtained as the mean phenol coefficient (Phenol Coefficient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example calculation provided (e.g., ((1.10/4.00) + (0.7/2.0))/2 = 0.31). Use the mean of the two contact-period coefficients as the final reported value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard incubation/time entries when reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report incubation time and temperature for each set (example entries: many rows show '7 days. 37 deg. C.' or '24 hours. 37 deg. C.' depending on results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the example table (Table 27) for formatting and interpreting time-to-growth entries across strengths and contact times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of metric units and prefixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the metric system units: metre (m) as unit of length, gramme (g) as unit of mass, litre (l) as unit of capacity. Use Latin prefixes milli = 1/1000, centi = 1/100, deci = 1/10; Greek prefixes deka = 10, hecto = 100, kilo = 1000, myria = 10,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual uses metric definitions and conversion factors throughout; adopt these definitions for preparing media and solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common conversion factors between metric and imperial
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide and use conversion factors (examples): 1 millimetre = 1/25 inch; 1 centimetre = 2/5 inch; 1 gramme = 15.4323 grains; 1 kgm = 2 pounds 3-1/4 ounces avoirdupois; 1 cubic centimetre = 16.9 minims; 1 litre = 35.196 fl. oz. imperial; 1 inch = 25 mm etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the provided lists and tables when converting between systems; follow the factors given for laboratory calculations and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for preparing a desired percentage of a given salt in tubed media
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the formula: (N + X) Y / 100 = A (X) / 100, where N = number of cubic centimetres in each tube, X = amount of stock solution to be added, Y = percentage required in the medium, A = percentage of stock solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: to make 4% KNO3 in 10 c.c. tubes from 25% stock: (10 + X) * 4 / 100 = 25 * X / 100, solve to obtain X = 1.9 c.c. (so 10 c.c. broth + 1.9 c.c. 25% stock). This allows for volume addition to original bulk of medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended scale increments for preparing serial dilutions
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing series of dilutions adhere to a definite scale of increments: from 1:10 to 1:80 rise by increments of 5; 1:80 to 1:200 rise by increments of 10; 1:200 to 1:400 rise by increments of 25; 1:400 to 1:500 rise by increments of 50; 1:500 to 1:1000 rise by increments of 100; 1:1000 to 1:5000 rise by increments of 250; 1:5000 to 1:10,000 rise by increments of 1000; 1:10,000 to 1:100,000 rise by increments of 5000; 1:100,000 to 1:1,000,000 rise by increments of 100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These scales economize labour while giving useful resolution across different potency ranges (especially for unknown-strength substances like agglutinating sera).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary dilution method examples (first to fourth dilutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary dilutions: FIRST (I): 1 c.c. serum + 9 c.c. normal saline = 10% solution or 1:10 dilution. SECOND (II): 1 c.c. first dilution + 9 c.c. = 1% or 1:100. THIRD (III): 1 c.c. second + 9 c.c. = 1:1000. FOURTH (IV): 1 c.c. second + 9 c.c. = 1:10,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these primary dilutions as stock for preparing secondary dilutions; when dealing with fluids other than serum use distilled water as diluent; for solids give analogous weight/volume instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables I–IV for preparing secondary dilutions from stock solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided tabular recipes (Tables I–IV) to prepare secondary dilutions from 10% stock, 1% stock, 0.1% stock, or 0.01% stock solutions (examples: 1:20 = 1 c.c. + 1.0 c.c. from 10% stock; 1:200 = 1 c.c. + 1.0 c.c. from 1% stock; 1:1000 = 1 c.c. + 0 c.c. from 0.1% stock etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the tables to avoid unnecessary calculations; note bracketed/omitted entries where approximate values are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature–pressure and desiccation reference tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the supplied tables converting centigrade temperatures to mm. Hg, pounds per sq. in. absolute pressure, and atmospheres, and tables for desiccation at low temperatures in vacuo (mm. of Hg at 21–50°C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference these tables for autoclave/steriliser/vacuo work and to set correct pressures/temperatures in physical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antiformin preparation and Antiformin method for B. tuberculosis detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare Antiformin: mix Eau de Javelle (Liquor sodae chlorinatae—B.P.) 50 c.c. and sodic hydrate 15% aqueous solution 50 c.c. Method: introduce specimen into a sterile tube, add equal volume of antiformin, close and shake vigorously; incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes (shaking from time to time); centrifugalise at high speed; pipette off supernatant and fill up with sterile distilled water, shake and re-centrifugalise; repeat steps 4 and 5 twice more; use one portion to inoculate guinea pigs and plant remainder on Dorset's Egg medium and incubate at 37°C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antiformin rapidly disintegrates associated bacteria while acid-fast tubercle bacilli resist; note: if only microscopical films are needed, fill centrifuge tube with Ligroin instead of distilled water in washing and prepare films from the surface for Ziehl–Neelsen staining.
